messages:
Sam: quick sync — we need to pick a benchmark approach for the kernel selection + microbatch SLO work. replay vs synthetic, how we handle KV cache priming, and how to report p95/p99 without getting whipsawed. opinions?
Maya: replay is closer to reality for KV cache behavior. long-context tails matter (KV hotness, prefix reuse). but replay is noisy and brittle to traffic changes.
Liam: +1 for doing both. synth for controlled sweeps (batch sizes, seq len), replay for validating the tail and cache effects. keep synth for perf regressions that need low variance.
Tess: hybrid works. plan: use replay to capture distribution & warmup, then run targeted synth cases to isolate kernel/batching dim. I'll add a short loadgen recipe.
Tess: ```
# synth sweep example
loadgen --model xformer_v2 --concurrency 64 --batch-sizes 1,4,8,16,32 --seq-dist zipf --kv-ttl 300
```
Raj: important: how we compute p95/p99 matters. sliding windows, bootstrap CIs, and removing cold-starts. if we publish a single p99 without CI we'll get blamed when it flips.
Maya: FYI prof results from yesterday: switching to kernel-opt B reduced avg time at large batches, but increased p99 at microbatch=1 and 4 (KV lock contention + kernel launch overhead). we should capture per-kernel breakdown.
Maya: short log snippet: ```
[profile] microbatch=4 kernel_A: 2.3ms kernel_B: 5.8ms kv-hit: 0.12ms kv-miss: 1.7ms
```
Liam: that suggests a threshold where kernel_B amortizes only when batch>=8 or when KV hit-rate > ~0.6. we should derive decision boundary: if expected batchwidth * kernel_B_gain > kernel_B_overhead then switch.
Sam: good — propose experiment plan: 1) replay baseline (24h) to capture tail and KV patterns; 2) synth sweep to get deterministic kernel latency surfaces; 3) small canary rollout with A/B routing and automatic fallback if p99 > SLO. owners?
Tess: I can run the replay on reserved infra and collect traces + per-token breakdowns. prefer to pin traffic dump to last 7 days with anonymization. :+1:
Liam: I'll implement synth harness + scripts that compute bootstrap CI for p95/p99. output JSON includes sample size and CI.
Maya: I'll add per-kernel flamegraphs and a heatmap of KV hit-rate vs tail latency. also capture GC/driver stalls.
Raj: I'll own the rollout policy and the alerting thresholds (p99 margin, consecutive violation window). recommend: p99 soft SLO = target*1.3, hard = target*2 before rollback.
ops-bot: perf-ci:kernel-sweep/1769999999 finished — regressions detected on microbatch=1 (p99 +18%). See: https://ci.redwood/perf/1769999999
Sam: perfect. thanks all — next sync Friday after initial replay run.
